topic: EXP-496 P1 verification — Cross-tab structure reading-guide paragraph appended to part1 Overview

The intent was to inoculate against the c2 HOL-REDUNDANCY hole 6 framing critique and pre-stage the cross-reference scaffolding subsequent spoke-consolidation EXPs will need.

holes_found.description:
Patch P1 is duplicated in data/sections.json AND in the built docs/index.html. After commit 08c3891 (decider-2026-06-01: EXP-496 reading-guide paragraph), part1.html contains TWO copies of the 'Cross-tab structure' paragraph (substring count 2; first occurrence at character index 6433, second at 8049, gap 1616 — i.e., the new paragraph and its near-identical twin). Substring counts confirmed in both data/sections.json and docs/index.html. Root cause: the 'Cross-tab structure' paragraph was already present in sections.json BEFORE the decider's EXP-496 run — it was introduced in commit e56d4b7 ('Update review (auto-build 2026-06-01)', 2026-06-01 13:19 UTC, +1 occurrence). The decider's subsequent EXP-496 application at 15:17 UTC re-applied the find-replace because find_text was unchanged (the prior 'This ordering is deliberate ... progressively broader domains.

' anchor is the same anchor the e56d4b7 paragraph attached to), and the patch inserted a SECOND copy. The decider's processed-proposals.json entry for ISS-2329 was supposed to gate this, but the dual-write pathway (auto-build commit at 13:19 inserting prose directly, then decider re-applying the same EXP at 15:17) bypassed it. Net effect: the paragraph specifically authored to inoculate the document against the 'repetitive' defender charge appears twice — exactly the charge it was designed to neutralize. A dome defender can fairly turn this around: 'You added a paragraph to address that the review is repetitive, and you added it twice.'
holes_found.recommendation: Decider: (1) remove ONE of the two copies in data/sections.json — keep the e56d4b7-inserted copy at idx 8049 (it has the \n\n separator and is what the build process committed first), drop the 08c3891-inserted copy at idx 6433 (the decider's duplicate). Or vice versa — both are byte-identical content; pick whichever leaves the cleanest diff. (2) Rebuild and verify substring count of 'Cross-tab structure' in data/sections.json drops to 1 and likewise in docs/index.html. (3) File a follow-up ISS to investigate the auto-build pathway: how did e56d4b7 modify sections.json directly (it shows 2 added lines / 128 removed lines, and one of the 2 added lines contains the Cross-tab paragraph), and what synchronization with the decider's processed-proposals.json is missing? This is a process bug that could repeat for any future EXP that lands via both auto-build and decider self-apply. (4) Run tests/run.sh after the de-duplication.

holes_found.description: Forward-looking framing overstates current state. The new paragraph asserts 'the cross-references above mark the canonical statement, with other appearances now serving as one-line pointers.' But EXP-496's own summary_for_decider explicitly states 'No spoke consolidation work is done in this EXP — that remains hole 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 6 scope in separate EXPs.' Per the kernel_of_truth count in the EXP, Part 4 still has 144 mentions of eclipse non-discrimination, Part 6 has 85, Part 8 has 13, Part 8b has 39 — these are far from being trimmed to 'one-line pointers.' A literal-minded defender (or AI auditor) following the paragraph's advice will find the spokes are NOT yet one-line pointers and conclude the paragraph misrepresents the state of consolidation.
holes_found.recommendation: Soften the framing from 'now serving as one-line pointers' to 'with other appearances pointing back to those hubs as consolidation lands' or 'with subsequent appearances scheduled for trimming to one-line pointers in companion EXPs (ISS-2329 family).' This change is honest about the in-flight consolidation and removes the gap between claim and observable state. Trivial diff.

holes_found.description: Lens enumeration omits Part 8b ('The Dome Author's Fair-Auditor List') and includes Part 9 ('Conclusions') as a 'lens'. Part 9 is a summary, not an analytical lens applying a separate analytical method. Part 8b IS a distinct analytical lens (it walks through the dome author's own published auditor instructions and asks 'what changes if we follow them') and arguably deserves a place in the list more than Part 9. The current enumeration reads 'AI-context directives (Part 8), and surviving conclusions (Part 9)' — neat-sounding but slightly mis-categorizing two of the ten parts. Not a defender hook on its own, but the paragraph's purpose is to be a navigation aid for a careful reader, and a careful reader will notice this.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: re-list as '... AI-context directives (Part 8), the dome's own fair-auditor instructions audited (Part 8b), and surviving conclusions (Part 9)' OR drop Part 9 from the lens list and let the rendered roadmap section above carry the role of 'find Part 9' for the reader. Decider's call; the wording works as-is but a careful reader will mark it.

stronger_arguments.description: If the decider de-duplicates per the major hole's recommendation, the surviving paragraph would benefit from naming the paragraph itself as an inoculation against the defender charge — e.g., open with 'Cross-tab structure (and why this review reads as repetitive).' That makes the meta-purpose explicit and gives the careful reader a clear pointer to the structural argument the paragraph is doing.

The five canonical hubs named in the paragraph (§4.2 eclipse, §1.5 aetheric refraction, §2.9 Sydney–Perth, §2b.2 relabeling, Timestamp Error tab OTS) are committed designations now that the paragraph names them. Future spoke-consolidation EXPs that re-route a hub designation (e.g., promoting §6.10 to be the canonical Sydney–Perth hub instead of §2.9) must EITHER edit this paragraph's hub list OR rebut the would-be replacement. Add a note to the EXP-496-family follow-up plan recording the implicit hub commitment.

kernel_of_truth.description: The reading-guide paragraph's core architectural insight — that the review applies a small set of analytical lenses across many tabs, and that recurring arguments are recurrence-across-lenses rather than within-each-lens redundancy — IS the right framing for the document's structure (data/sections.json:part1 evidence-roadmap; HOL-REDUNDANCY.c2:hole_6_recommendation). The five hub designations (§4.2 eclipse, §1.5 aetheric refraction, §2.9 Sydney–Perth, §2b.2 relabeling, Timestamp Error tab OTS) match what the c2 review explicitly recommended (HOL-REDUNDANCY.c2:holes_0_1_2_4_6) and what EXP-495 already used when consolidating Sydney–Perth content. The anchor-link mechanics resolve correctly in the built output (docs/index.html: id-counts 1/1/1/1/1 for the five anchors, verified). When de-duplicated, the paragraph is a useful navigation scaffold that pre-empts a real defender charge without conceding the redundancy is content padding.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The duplication itself is the kernel-busting irony: the paragraph designed to inoculate against the 'repetitive' charge by explaining that recurrence is across-lenses-not-within-lenses (data/sections.json:part1, paragraph at idx 6433 AND idx 8049 — both verbatim copies) appears verbatim TWICE on the same page (substring count 2 in both data/sections.json and docs/index.html). For the inoculation to land, the paragraph must demonstrate the discipline it preaches. Until commit 08c3891's duplicate is removed, the paragraph self-falsifies. Separately, the 'now serving as one-line pointers' framing overstates the current consolidation state (per EXP-496.summary_for_decider's own acknowledgment that 'No spoke consolidation work is done in this EXP' and the kernel_of_truth count of 144/85/13/39 unconsolidated mentions across Parts 4/6/8/8b for the eclipse cluster alone), so even a de-duplicated paragraph will need a minor tense softening before it is fully load-bearing.

deeper_analysis:
The decider's queue-push classified this item as class='verification' but EXP-496's authored review_class was 'deep-attack' (rationale in the EXP: 'the cross-reference framing is new argumentative content, not refinement of existing prose'). Per PROP-025, the decider is supposed to propagate the analyst's review_class to the queue at integration time; it did not. The class mismatch is the immediate process bug that allowed this item to be eligible for verify-mode handoff and for curmudgeon batching, both of which would have produced a less-thorough review and likely missed the duplication. Recommend the decider audit its review_class propagation step for the EXP-496 integration and similar integrations going forward — when an EXP introduces new argumentative content (especially a load-bearing inoculation paragraph at the document head), the queue class must be 'deep-attack' so the curmudgeon's run gets full attention. The duplication itself was the more visible bug, but the misclassification was the gating condition that nearly let the duplication slip through unnoticed.

A further consideration: the new paragraph commits the project to five canonical-hub designations (§4.2 / §1.5 / §2.9 / §2b.2 / Timestamp Error tab). The c2 HOL-REDUNDANCY hole 6 stronger_arguments recommendation explicitly framed this as the consolidation scaffolding, so the hub commitment is intentional, not accidental. Future EXPs touching these hubs (a candidate set: any of holes 0–4 of HOL-REDUNDANCY.c2 still open) inherit the constraint that they must either keep the named hub or justify a replacement. That is a reasonable scaffolding discipline and not a hole; it is just a forward-binding consequence the decider should track in the issues for those holes.

On the other side: a charitable read says the duplicate paragraph is harmless. It is byte-identical content, so a reader who skims past the first paragraph will read the second and get the same payload; the only cost is roughly 1.6 KB of extra HTML and one extra mental 'wait, did I just read that?' beat. Severity could be argued as moderate rather than major on that view. I rated it major because (a) the paragraph's stated purpose is to inoculate against the 'repetitive' defender charge, which is empirically falsified the moment the paragraph appears twice; (b) commit 08c3891's commit message states the patch added the paragraph 'under the existing How This Review Is Organized h2', implying the decider believed it was inserting once — the gap between intent and result is itself a process integrity finding, not just a cosmetic glitch; and (c) the decider's deduplication is straightforward (a one-line edit), so the cost of treating it as major and routing it back through the queue is low.

The patch's find_text anchor was still unique post-e56d4b7, so the find-replace happily inserted a second copy. Process fix: investigate why the e56d4b7 auto-build commit modified sections.json directly with the new paragraph (commit shows +2 / -128 lines, including the Cross-tab paragraph as one of the additions); this dual-write pathway bypasses processed-proposals.json deduplication and will repeat for any future EXP that lands via both manual auto-build and decider self-apply. Per PROP-025, the decider must propagate the analyst's review_class; the downgrade allowed this item to be eligible for verify-mode handoff and for curmudgeon batching, either of which would have likely missed the duplication. Recommend decider audit its review_class propagation step. MINOR finding 1: 'now serving as one-line pointers' overstates current consolidation state (per EXP-496.summary_for_decider's own acknowledgment that no spoke consolidation work is done in this EXP). MINOR finding 2: lens enumeration omits Part 8b and includes Part 9 (a summary, not a lens). Anchor mechanics verified clean in the built output (5/5 anchors resolve).
